description: Golden cases for drift detection. Data side: sandboxed scans of the built-in vulnerable target and fixed findings fixtures, compared to recorded baselines. Model side: the production executive-summary prompt, checked deterministically and by an LLM judge (score >= thresholds.min_judge_score). Re-capture baselines only after an intentional scanner change: python -m pentest_agent.evals.golden --record-baseline must_not_mention holds only phrases that are wrong in any context (substring checks cannot see negation); severity inflation and unsupported claims are scored by the judge's faithfulness.

cases.description: Standard (active) scan of the built-in vulnerable target: all 14 planted issues must be found and the summary must lead with the high-severity ones.

required_titles: Password form served over plaintext HTTP
titles: CORS reflects arbitrary Origin with credentials
POST form without apparent anti-CSRF token
Password form served over plaintext HTTP
Possible SQL injection (database error on quote)
Reflected input without output encoding (possible XSS)

cases.reference_summary: The authorized standard-profile test of the target crawled the in-scope pages and found seven high-severity issues that need prompt remediation: a possible SQL injection on the product page, a path traversal that disclosed a local file, an exposed .env file, CORS that reflects any origin with credentials, and client-side JavaScript containing a hardcoded secret, an AWS access key and use of eval. Medium-severity issues include reflected input without output encoding (possible XSS), an open redirect, directory listing, a password form served over plain HTTP, an enabled TRACE method, a session cookie without HttpOnly, and a missing Content-Security-Policy. Lower-severity items are missing hardening headers, a POST form without an anti-CSRF token and weak randomness in JavaScript. Each statement cites its source finding. Fix the injection, traversal and exposed secrets first, rotate any leaked keys, then apply header and cookie hardening. Results come from automated checks and should be validated before disclosure.

cases.description: Quick (passive-only) scan of the same target: no active-attack findings may appear, and the summary must not claim injection or traversal issues.

titles: CORS reflects arbitrary Origin with credentials
POST form without apparent anti-CSRF token
Password form served over plaintext HTTP

cases.reference_summary: This passive (quick) test examined the in-scope pages without sending attack payloads, so injection-style issues were not tested. It still found high-severity exposure: an accessible .env environment file, CORS that reflects arbitrary origins with credentials, and client-side JavaScript containing a hardcoded secret, an AWS access key and use of eval. Medium-severity issues include directory listing, a password form over plaintext HTTP, a session cookie without HttpOnly, the TRACE method enabled and a missing Content-Security-Policy, with lower-severity header hardening gaps. Each claim cites its source finding. Remove the exposed files and secrets first, then harden headers and cookies, and run a standard-profile test for active coverage.

cases.description: Fixed two-finding input (no scan): the summary must stay within these facts and not inflate severity.

input_findings.title: Reflected input without output encoding (possible XSS)
input_findings.description: The q parameter on /search is reflected into HTML without encoding '<', '"' or '''.
input_findings.recommendation: HTML-encode untrusted output and add a Content-Security-Policy.

input_findings.title: Missing X-Content-Type-Options header
input_findings.description: Responses do not send X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.
input_findings.recommendation: Send X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on all responses.

titles: Reflected input without output encoding (possible XSS)

cases.reference_summary: An automated standard-profile test of https://golden.example.test crawled 3 in-scope pages and produced two findings, neither critical nor high. The most significant is a medium-severity reflected-input issue on the search page: the q parameter is echoed into HTML without output encoding, which may allow cross-site scripting [S1]. The second is a low-severity hardening gap: responses omit the X-Content-Type-Options header [S2]. No red flags were raised. Recommended next steps are to HTML-encode untrusted output and add a Content-Security-Policy, then send X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. The XSS finding should be confirmed manually before disclosure.

cases.reference_summary: A passive (quick-profile) automated test of https://clean.example.test crawled 4 in-scope pages and produced no findings and no red flags. This means none of the passive checks flagged an issue; it does not prove the application is secure, because the quick profile sends no active test payloads and authenticated areas were not assessed. A standard-profile test and periodic re-testing are recommended for broader coverage.
